name: Pacific & Indian cyclones
summary: Cyclone Murasu, a GDACS red alert, crossed the Andhra Pradesh coast near Ongole early on 3 Nov
state: Severe cyclonic storm Murasu crossed the south Andhra Pradesh coast near Ongole at about 01:00 local time on 3 Nov with winds of 100–110km/h gusting to 120km/h, according to the India Meteorological Department (India TV). Heavy rain was forecast for another 12 hours and a 1–1.5m storm surge for Bapatla, Krishna and Prakasam districts; no deaths had been reported. GDACS still listed a red alert on 3 Nov.
for_you: Travellers to Andhra Pradesh, Odisha and Tamil Nadu should follow India Meteorological Department warnings and FCDO travel advice, and expect flight cancellations.
rubric_hit: GDACS red cyclone alert (Murasu); severe cyclone landfall on a populated coast = Alert

why: Typhoons and cyclones are the deadliest weather events, threatening densely populated coasts in Asia and the Indian Ocean.
drivers: Ocean heat, ENSO phase, season (W Pacific peaks Jul–Oct; N Indian Apr–Jun & Oct–Dec).

rubric.alert: GDACS red cyclone alert, or a super-typhoon/severe cyclone landfall on a populated coast.
rubric.watch: GDACS orange cyclone alert, or a typhoon/cyclone threatening land within 72h.
rubric.normal: No GDACS orange/red tropical cyclone alerts.
